explain.say: The trigger is day length, not cold. As autumn days shorten, the eyes sense less light, and the brain makes more of the hormone melatonin during the longer nights, which sets off a moult.

faq.q: How do animals know when to change colour?
faq.a: They measure day length. Shortening autumn days change the amount of the hormone melatonin the brain makes at night, which triggers the moult to white; lengthening spring days trigger the moult back to brown.
asks: Does cold make animals turn white?

faq.q: Why do arctic animals turn white?
faq.a: White hides them against snow, helping hares and ptarmigan escape predators and helping foxes and stoats sneak up on prey. Their winter coat is also thicker and warmer.
asks: Why is the arctic fox white in winter?

faq.a: White hairs contain no coloured pigment, and they are full of tiny air spaces that scatter all colours of light equally, so they look white, just like snow.

faq.q: Which animals change colour with the seasons?
faq.a: Arctic foxes, stoats, weasels in snowy areas, snowshoe and mountain hares, collared lemmings and ptarmigan all turn white in winter. Populations living where snow is rare often stay brown all year.
asks: Which birds turn white in winter?

faq.a: Camouflage mismatch is when an animal's colour no longer matches its background, like a white hare on brown ground after snow melts early. Mismatched animals are easier for predators to see.
